label: Ubiquiti UniFi 5G Max Modem
description: 5G NR/LTE modem for UniFi: one 2.5GbE RJ45, PoE input, nano-SIM or eSIM.
notes: Vendor figures from the Ubiquiti tech specs page: Networking Interface **(1) 2.5 GbE RJ45 port**, **5G NR and LTE** radio, nano-SIM or eSIM, PoE input, IK04 tamper resistance, 410 g. The 2.5G port is the point: it will not bottleneck a 5G NR link the way a gigabit port would, which is exactly the difference from the plain U5G. **Radio rates from the same page, read 2026-11-19:** 5G NSA downlink **3.4 Gbps** / uplink 560 Mbps, 5G SA 1.8 Gbps / 650 Mbps, 4G LTE 1.6 Gbps / 210 Mbps, **(4) embedded cellular antennas**. `wwan0` used to carry `1G`, which the engine ladder resolves to [lte, lte-a] - a 5G NR modem with no 5G NR medium to cable - while the UDR-5G-Max, the same radio, carried 3.4G. It now carries 3.4G, the vendor 5G NSA downlink figure, so 5g-sub6 is offered. Sources: https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/accessories/u5g-max (200, 691,340 B) and https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/integrations/u5g-max (200, same table), both served 2026-11-19. The plain U5G stays at 100M: it is 5G RedCap and Ubiquiti publishes no RedCap rate to cite.
